AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 1.
A DAR was filed on 28/02/2018 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of the parties of this case.

The said DAR was related to a motor vehicular accident dated 12/11/2017 in which one Sh.
Kewal Krishan S/o Sh. Gopal Krishan (hereinafter referred to PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.02.15 14:35:18 +0530 as "petitioner") sustained grievous injuries.

Subsequent to the filing of DAR, the present petition was filed on 31/07/2018 U/s 166 r/w Section 140 of M.V.
Act seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 8,00,000/- under Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 in respect of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a motor vehicular accident which took place on 12/11/2017 behind Udham Singh School, Shastri Nagar, Delhi falling within the jurisdiction of PS Sarai Rohilla, Delhi.

As per this petition, at the relevant time the petitioner was going to the market for some household articles on his Scooty bearing registration no. DL-4SDG-7770 and when he reached at the spot of accident the respondent while driving his motorcycle (Pulsar Balck) bearing registration no. DL-6SAC-9017 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") rashly, negligently and at a very fast speed hit the petitioner and the petitioner fell down on the road badly injured.
It is further stated that the petitioner was taken to the HRH Hospital vide MLC No. 7043/17 and further the petitioner was taken to Town Phase IX for further proper treatment.
An FIR No. 431/17 PS Sarai Rohilla U/s 279/338 IPC was registered by the police.
Petitioner claims that he was 24 years of age at the time of accident and was self employed and was earning Rs. 22,000/- per month.
It is further stated that the petitioner has been under treatment for more than 06 months and is taking physiotherapy at present and he has spent more than Rs.7,50,000/- for his treatment.
Respondent is stated to be the driver- cum-owner of the offending vehicle.
Respondent was directed to file his written statement.
PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA
A written statement was filed by respondent in which he denied the contents of the petition.

ISSUE NO.1 "Whether the petitioner Sh. Kewal Krishan suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 12.11.2017 involving Motorcycle (Black Pulsar) bearing registration No. DL-6SAC-9017 driven rashly and negligently and owned by the Respondent?

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.02.15 14:35:42 +0530 under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. &
Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of respondent in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold respondent guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
13. In view of the medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.

This issue thus stands decided against the respondent and in favour of the petitioner.

15. As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non- pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.

and the PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.02.15 14:36:05 +0530 non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings,
loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair,
reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India)
Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 243.

The petitioner has placed on judicial file the medical treatment records and bills as Ex. PW1/3 (colly) and Ex. PW1/2 (colly).

As per the said documents, petitioner has incurred expenses to the tune of Rs. 1,75,093.19/- In the absence of any contest to the said documents (placed on record by the petitioner), the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs.1,75,093/- (rounded off) under this head.
(ii) Pain and Suffering 19.
As per MLC annexed alongwith the DAR, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.
which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.
Thus, he is awarded a total amount of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.02.15 14:36:16 +0530 (iii) Loss of actual earnings 20.
In his affidavit Ex. PW1/A, the petitioner claims that he was self employed at the time of accident and was earning Rs.22,000/- per month from that vocation.
The medical records placed on record by petitioner reflect that the petitioner sustained a grievous injuries.
The above documents are sufficient to uphold the claim of the petitioner to the effect that he was unable to resume his work since the date of accident.
As per record, the petitioner has not filed any documentary proof regarding his employment and income.
Also, the petitioner ha snot filed any documentary proof regarding his loss of income.
In view of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner could not have worked for about 03 months due to the injuries.
Accordingly, the Minimum Wages admissible to a Unskilled Person as on 12.11.2017 in Delhi the earnings was Rs.13,584/-.

As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs.40,752/-
(Rs.13,584/- X 3).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
(iv) Conveyance, Attendant Charges, Special Diet and amenities of life 21.
In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs. 35,000/- each under these heads.

7. I have perused the record and my issue wise findings is as under:-
ISSUE NO.1 "Whether the petitioner Sh. Kewal Krishan suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 12.11.2017 involving Motorcycle (Black Pulsar) bearing registration No. DL-6SAC-9017 driven rashly and negligently and owned by the Respondent?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
8. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.02.15 14:35:42 +0530 under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. &
Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.
There is nothing on record which betrays any falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW-1.
As such, it could be safely held that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.
10. The very fact that R-1 has already been chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC in the above criminal case/FIR in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW1 and the case of petitioner on this issue.
view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
12.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time, respondent was driving the offending vehicle a in rash and negligent manner in a high speed at the relevant time.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of respondent in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold respondent guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non- pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair,
reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.
Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India)
Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 243.
PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.02.15 14:36:11 +0530 17.
It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.
which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.
